items.title: Police receive 87 reports, open 23 investigation papers in Negeri Sembilan election campaign
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) received 87 reports and opened 23 investigation papers involving alleged election offences during the campaign period for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election from July 18 until yesterday. Negeri Sembilan Police Chief DCP Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said 761 out of 787 permit applications submitted for ceramah and political campaign activities during the same period were approved. For the latest news on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9 .

items.title: Anwar sends well‑wishes to Sultan Ibrahim ahead of medical treatment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has offered prayers for the good health of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who is set to undergo medical treatment. “May His Majesty be blessed with continued good health and remain under the protection and mercy of Allah,” Anwar said in a Facebook post today. Earlier, Istana Negara announced that Sultan Ibrahim would undergo follow-up treatment for a musculoskeletal condition involving His Majesty’s back and hip.

items.title: RCI report on Tabung Haji to be published in full, says Anwar
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would not redact any part of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH). He said the report would be published in full, including all recommendations and processes undertaken, with its scope extended beyond the original period covered to examine developments after 2020. Anwar said the RCI report itself covered developments from 2014, when Bank Negara Malaysia first issued an early warning.

items.title: Partial lane closures in Penang for LRT works on Jalan Kampung Relau, Tun Dr Awang from Aug 1
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 31 — Intermittent partial lane closures along Jalan Kampung Relau and Jalan Tun Dr. Awang will be implemented for 75 days from tomorrow to facilitate drainage and road widening works for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) Project. “The affected areas involve the leftmost lane in front of Penang International Commercial City (PICC) towards Bayan Lepas, the leftmost lane in front of the Petron Bukit Jambul petrol station heading towards Komtar and the leftmost lane from the Jalan Tun Dr. Awang entry slip road to Jalan Kampung Relau and SMK Sungai Nibong heading towards Komtar. MRT Corp said the closure was necessary to facilitate preliminary works under the Mutiara Line LRT Project’s CMC1 Package, involving drainage and road widening works.

items.title: Cyberjaya gets Malaysia’s first autonomous vehicle control centre ahead of Level 4 trials
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, July 31 — Malaysia’s first Remote Operations Centre (ROC) for autonomous logistics vehicles has been launched in Cyberjaya, paving the way for Level 4 autonomous vehicle trials on public roads. The facility at CoPlace 9 Cyberjaya was developed by Autonomous Logistic Solutions Sdn Bhd (ALS) in collaboration with the Selangor Information Technology & Digital Economy Corporation (Sidec) and Cyberview Sdn Bhd, and will support trials along the 22km Cyberjaya Malaysia Autonomous Vehicle (MyAV) Route. ALS managing director Alan Chong said the ROC would provide oversight for the company’s Level 4 autonomous logistics vehicle, the RoboVan, during upcoming trials.

items.title: Negri polls: 87 reports received, 23 probe papers opened
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Police received 87 reports and opened 23 investigation papers involving alleged election offences during the campaign period for the 16th Negeri Sembilan Election from July 18 until yesterday. Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said 761 of 787 permit applications submitted for ceramah and political campaign activities during the period were approved. Alzafny said police would continue to strengthen preparedness and enforcement efforts, adding that any violation of the law would be dealt with firmly and fairly.

items.title: Sabah JKR: Structural damage forces closure of Jalan Tun Fuad Stephen bridge in Kota Kinabalu
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 31 — The bridge at Kilometre 2.850 of Jalan Tun Fuad Stephen here will be closed from noon today after an inspection detected serious structural damage to its concrete deck. The Sabah Public Works Department (JKR), in a statement today, said the closure was necessary to ensure the safety of road users. “The closure affects the route from Kota Kinabalu City towards Teluk Likas and will be lifted once the temporary diversion works are completed.

items.title: Drugged Malaysian pilot risks death penalty for smuggling in Indonesia
items.summary: JAKARTA: A Malaysian pilot who tested positive for meth, MDMA, and cocaine after flying a passenger plane to Indonesia risks the death penalty for allegedly smuggling more than 70,000 ecstasy tablets in his suitcase, officials said Friday. The 39-year-old pilot, identified only by his initials, MSO, was arrested Wednesday at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta international airport shortly after arriving from Kuala Lumpur. The airport customs office did not say which carrier the pilot worked for, but the flight number indicated it was a Malaysia Airlines plane.

items.title: Sarawak-level Warriors’ Day parade in Petra Jaya honours fallen heroes
items.summary: The 2026 Sarawak-level Warriors’ Day Parade, organised by the First Infantry Division of the Malaysian Army in collaboration with the Royal Malaysia Police Sarawak Contingent, brought together personnel from the armed forces, police, and veterans in honour of those who had defended the country’s sovereignty. Sarawak Governor Tun Pehin Sri Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar and his wife Toh Puan Datuk Patinggi Fauziah Mohd Sanusi graced the event, which was also attended by Minister for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Dato Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, who represented the Premier, Sarawak police commissioner CP Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, and First Infantry Division commander Maj Gen Mohd Sobirin Mohd Yusof. — Mohd Faisal Ahmad/The Borneo Post pic A total of 460 personnel from four detachments took part in the parade, led by commanding officer of the 10th Border Regiment Lt Col Ferry Shahrul Rizal Roslan, accompanied by the Combined Drum Platoon of the 4th Royal Armoured Corps Regiment, 13th Royal Malay Regiment Battalion and the 20th Royal Malay Regiment Battalion.

items.title: Riyadh Air launches thrice weekly Riyadh-Kuala Lumpur flight
items.summary: SEPANG: Riyadh Air has launched a three-times-weekly flight between Riyadh and Kuala Lumpur, making the Malaysian capital its first destination in Southeast Asia. Riyadh Air chief executive officer Tony Douglas said Kuala Lumpur represented an important step in the airline's international expansion. "Today's inaugural flight to Kuala Lumpur is a defining moment for Riyadh Air as we establish our footprint in Southeast Asia.

items.title: North Korea growth topped 3pct for third straight year in 2025: Seoul
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea's economy grew more than three per cent for a third straight year in 2025, South Korea's central bank estimated Friday, as Pyongyang continues to deepen economic and military ties with Russia. The isolated North's real gross domestic product expanded 3.5 per cent to 38.26 trillion (US$26.6 billion) won last year, the Bank of Korea said in its report. "The expansion of economic cooperation with Russia was a major driver of North Korea's growth last year," a BoK official told AFP.

items.title: MACC receives four reports of alleged cash handouts in Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 31 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has received four reports related to alleged cash handouts during the Negeri Sembilan State Election. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the reports, received yesterday, involved two election candidates and two early voters. Abd Halim said the MACC would investigate whether the complaints contained elements of corruption or constituted election offences.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines conducting internal review after pilot arrested in Indonesia over drugs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines is conducting an internal review after a pilot was detained by Indonesian authorities over alleged narcotics-related offences. In a statement to Bernama today, Malaysia Airlines said it would not be appropriate to comment further as the matter remains under investigation by the Indonesian authorities. "Malaysia Airlines wishes to reiterate that it does not tolerate any form of misconduct and is conducting an internal review into the matter," it said.

items.title: Armed forces chief: Honour national heroes, instil patriotism in future generations
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Armed Forces Chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman has called on Malaysians to uphold patriotism and continue honouring the sacrifices of national heroes who defended the country's independence, sovereignty and peace. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, attended the ceremony. Also present were Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.

items.title: Families seek legal action over Sungai Pari Flats deaths
items.summary: IPOH: The families of two schoolgirls who died after falling from the abandoned Sungai Pari Flats in Buntong last week are seeking legal action against parties they claim failed to ensure the safety of the premises. The families of the two girls, both aged 14, alleged that the lack of proper security measures, including the absence of fencing around the 15-storey abandoned building, had exposed the public, including children, to danger. The families also called for immediate measures, including installing proper fencing around the abandoned flats, increasing police patrols and deploying more security personnel to monitor the area.

items.title: Two Indonesian men charged with trafficking 147kg meth in Malaysia
items.summary: BALIK PULAU, July 31 — Two Indonesian men were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with two counts of trafficking 147.188 kilogrammes of methamphetamine into the country two weeks ago. On the first charge, they are jointly accused of trafficking 113.776 kg of methamphetamine in the waters of Teluk Kumbar at about 7.15 pm on July 17 this year. They are also jointly charged with trafficking 33.412 kg of liquid methamphetamine at the same location, date, and time.

items.title: MyIMMs hack: Immigration Dept to revoke all fraudulently approved work passes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — The Immigration Department will revoke all Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) that were fraudulently approved through the hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs), its director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said today. The move is the department’s first step following the discovery of irregular PLKS approvals under Ops Crack, a joint operation with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), The Star reported. Zakaria said authorities would then track down all affected pass holders but declined to reveal their locations to avoid jeopardising the operation.

items.title: ITMAX secures RM120mil DBKL smart lighting contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ITMAX System Bhd has secured a RM120 million contract from Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to supply, install and maintain smart street lighting systems across Kuala Lumpur. ITMAX System managing director and chief executive officer William Tan Wei Lun said the award reflected DBKL's continued confidence in the group's capabilities and proven track record. "This award also recognises our locally designed and developed Malaysian smart street lighting system, demonstrating that home-grown innovation can deliver world-class smart city solutions.

items.title: Govt shifts focus to scaling up MSMEs after resilient 2025
items.summary: Despite outpacing the broader economy in 2025, more than three quarters of MSMEs remained micro enterprises, highlighting the need to help businesses scale up, improve productivity and expand into international markets, Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said. The sector outpaced Malaysia's overall economic growth of 5.2 per cent, with its contribution to GDP increasing to 39.7 per cent from 39.5 per cent in 2024. However, Sim said more than 77 per cent remained micro enterprises, while only 1.1 per cent were medium-sized businesses.

items.title: [UPDATED] Police confirm Malaysian pilot's arrest in Jakarta
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have confirmed that a 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was detained by Indonesian authorities for allegedly attempting to smuggle drugs through Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta. Federal police Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the man was arrested shortly after arriving in Jakarta from Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday night. () Reports by Kompas.com and Suara.com said Indonesian authorities also found 2.74g of methamphetamine, as well as 0.0825g of methamphetamine residue in a glass pipe, when the suspect was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport at about 11.30pm local time on Tuesday.

items.title: EV charging network must grow with adoption, says Johari
items.summary: Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the government is determined to ensure the country's EV ecosystem develops in tandem with vehicle sales, as inadequate charging facilities could undermine consumer confidence. The ministry is targeting 30,000 public EV chargers nationwide, although no timeline has been set. Johari said Malaysia currently has about 1,000 charging stations.

items.title: Police probe Facebook post allegedly insulting Perlis royal institution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Police have received two reports over a social media post allegedly containing insults against the Perlis royal institution related to the conferment of state honours. He said both complainants claimed they saw a post uploaded by a Facebook account user at 11.36pm yesterday. Yusharifuddin said the complainants believed the post could create negative perceptions towards the Perlis royal institution and potentially cause misunderstandings.

items.title: Anwar extends birthday greetings to Sultan of Pahang on 67th birthday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended his heartfelt congratulations to the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, on His Royal Highness’s 67th birthday. In a Facebook post today, Anwar prayed that the Sultan and the Pahang Royal Family would continue to be blessed with Allah’s mercy and guidance, and be granted good health, lasting wellbeing and enduring sovereignty. “Daulat Tuanku, Dirgahayu Tuanku,” he posted.

items.title: Negri polls: Anwar seeks continuity, stability in election appeal [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim appealed to Negri Sembilan voters to set aside political differences and give the unity government a fresh mandate as campaigning drew to a close ahead of tomorrow's state election. In a video message posted on his social media platforms today, Anwar said the campaign period may have been marked by "excesses" and called on voters to forgive one another. "So let us all apologise to one another and be friends again, because we are competing among fellow Malaysians, the residents of Negri Sembilan," he said.

items.title: Nga Kor Ming: Draft Real Property Development Act in final stage as part of housing reforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — A proposed Real Property Development Act is in the final stage of drafting as part of efforts to strengthen regulation of Malaysia’s property sector, according to Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga said the proposed legislation formed part of five housing reforms introduced by the ministry to improve governance and transparency in the property sector. He said the reforms also included the electronic sale and purchase agreement (eSPA), the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), the National Property Data System and regulated housing development accounts.

items.title: QR code immigration clearance system expands to 4 Sarawak border posts
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Home Ministry, in collaboration with the Sarawak government, will expand the MyNIISe QR code immigration clearance system to four major border checkpoints along the Sarawak-Brunei border starting tomorrow. "The system aims to expedite immigration checks, boost service efficiency and reinforce national border security," the Home Ministry said in a statement. It said the QR code clearance system would cover vehicle lanes across four key border posts, namely the Sungai Tujoh, Tedungan, Pandaruan and Mengkalap Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) complexes.

items.title: Housing Ministry to open big data platform for developers to match supply with demand, says Nga Kor Ming
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) is developing a big data analytics platform that will be opened to private developers to improve housing planning and address the mismatch between housing supply and market demand. Minister Nga Kor Ming said developers would be able to subscribe to the platform, enabling feasibility studies to be based on data and market demand rather than assumptions, as part of the ministry’s digital transformation efforts to create a more sustainable housing market. Nga said KPKT is also studying the housing needs of the M40 income group to ensure future housing products better match market demand.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin witnesses poignant tribute to Al-Maunah fallen heroes
items.summary: The performance revisited one of the country's most challenging security episodes — the 2000 armed standoff involving the Al-Maunah militant group, which claimed the lives of two security personnel. The stolen weapons were later taken to Bukit Jenalik in Sauk, Kuala Kangsar, where members of the Al-Maunah group camped, triggering a major security operation involving the Malaysian Armed Forces and police. As the standoff continued, security forces launched psychological operations on July 4 to persuade the militants to surrender.

items.title: MyIMMs hacking probe widens, more suspects on MACC radar
items.summary: MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the number of people involved could be considered large, with investigations still ongoing to determine the extent of their involvement, Malay daily Harian Metro reported today. “The operation involved the Special Projects Branch under MACC’s Intelligence Division, together with JIM’s Intelligence Division, the Securities Commission Malaysia, Telekom Malaysia, the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) and MACC’s Technology Forensics Division. Abd Halim said they comprised two company directors, three foreigners, four JIM officers, two officers from JIM’s Information Technology Division and one police officer.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines reserves comment, pledges full cooperation with Indonesian authorities on pilot’s alleged drug case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Malaysia Airlines reserves its comment on its pilot being caught for a narcotics-related offence by the Indonesian authorities but noted that the airline takes such allegations seriously. In a statement to Bernama today, the national carrier said Malaysia Airlines will extend its full cooperation to the relevant authorities in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations. According to Indonesia Customs and Excise director general Djaka Budi Utama, the pilot is under investigation in Indonesia for allegedly trying to traffic drugs including ecstasy worth about 60 billion rupiah (RM14 million).

items.title: Klang teen dies in LPT crash en route to RXZ Members 8.0 event in Terengganu
items.summary: He said initial investigations found the victim was travelling from Klang to Kuala Terengganu with a convoy of five motorcyclists to attend the event. “Upon reaching the location, the motorcycle ridden by the victim is believed to have skidded before falling on the left lane, causing the victim to be thrown onto the right lane. Mohd Nasyim said the victim was pronounced dead at the scene.

items.title: Immigration hack: Insiders exploited to breach MyIMMs system
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The syndicate suspected of hacking the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to unlawfully process Temporary Employment Visit Pass (PLKS) applications exploited insiders within the Immigration Department to gain access to the system. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation, uncovered under Op Crack, could not have been carried out without the involvement of people familiar with the department's systems. The operation involved the MACC, Immigration Department, Securities Commission Malaysia, Telekom Malaysia, National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and the MACC Technology Forensics Division.

items.title: N. Sembilan polls: EC says no complaints of vote‑buying during campaign
items.summary: TAMPIN, July 31 — The Election Commission (EC) has confirmed that it has not received any official complaints regarding allegations of money politics or bribery during the early voting period and the Negeri Sembilan state election campaign so far, said its chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun. According to Ramlan, his party recorded 267 election offences throughout the campaign period for the Negeri Sembilan election which began on July 18 and actions have already been taken. Meanwhile, he said all polling centres in Negeri Sembilan are on standby to receive voters who will be casting their ballots tomorrow.

items.title: 2 Filipinos jailed for illegal entry after murder probe detention
items.summary: Sessions Court Judge Hurman Hussain meted out the sentence to the two men, aged 39 and 21. The 39-year-old was arrested at about 2.30pm on July 16, 2026, at an open area in Kampung Numbak 2, Manggatal. The 21-year-old was arrested three days later, at about 3.20pm on July 19, by the roadside in Kampung Numbak, Sepanggar.

items.title: Malaysian pilot accused of smuggling 70,000 ecstasy tablets into Jakarta, risks death penalty, say Indonesian police
items.summary: JAKARTA, July 31 — A Malaysian pilot risks the death penalty in Indonesia after being arrested at Jakarta’s international airport with more than 70,000 ecstasy tablets in his suitcase, according to police who said today the man was on drugs while flying a passenger plane. The 39-year-old pilot, identified only by his initials, MSO, was arrested late Wednesday at Soekarno-Hatta international airport shortly after arriving from Kuala Lumpur. The airport customs office did not mention which airline the pilot worked for, but the flight number indicated it was a Malaysia Airlines plane.

items.title: EC: No official complaints over vote-buying in Negri polls
items.summary: TAMPIN: The Election Commission (EC) has not received any official complaints over allegations of vote-buying or bribery during early voting or the Negri Sembilan election campaign, says chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun. "We have not received any official complaints regarding bribery. Ramlan said the EC had recorded 267 election offences since campaigning began on July 18, with action taken in each case.

items.title: Prosecute those implicated in Tabung Haji RCI report, says consumer association
items.summary: Its president, Mohideen Abdul Kader, said the declassified RCI report exposed governance failures, political interference and financial misrepresentation that amounted to a betrayal of millions of depositors. Mohideen said the report had also damaged Malaysia's international standing as a leader in Islamic finance, noting that TH had long been regarded as a model for pilgrimage fund management and Islamic social finance. He said the RCI found that while TH reported a RM3.4 billion profit in 2017, proper financial reporting standards showed the fund had actually recorded a RM1.4 billion net loss, reflecting a RM4.8 billion discrepancy.

items.title: Najib questions selective trust in National Audit Department over TH issue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak today questioned what he described as selective judgement towards the National Audit Department over issues surrounding its findings on Tabung Haji (TH). See-To said the RCI itself acknowledged that TH's financial statements for 2014 to 2017 were issued with unqualified audit opinions by the National Audit Department. Why was the National Audit Department's acceptance of TH's asset valuation methods considered problematic?

items.title: Stats Dept: Malaysia’s economy expands 5.8pc in Q2 2026 as exports surge 45.3pc
items.summary: Malaysia’s industrial activity also remained strong, with the Industrial Production Index (IPI) increasing 8.4 per cent in May 2026, compared with 8.2 per cent growth in April. DOSM said the increase was mainly supported by the manufacturing sector, which grew 6.6 per cent, while the mining sector recorded stronger growth of 19.8 per cent, followed by the electricity sector with a 4.2 per cent expansion. On the external front, DOSM said total trade increased 29.8 per cent year-on-year to RM327.6 billion in May, supported by exports which jumped 45.3 per cent to RM184 billion.

items.title: Nga: Real Property Development Act in final drafting stage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed Real Property Development Act is in the final stage of drafting as part of efforts to strengthen regulation of Malaysia's property sector, says Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga said the Act formed part of five housing reforms introduced by the ministry to improve governance and transparency in the property sector. The reforms also include the electronic sale and purchase agreement (eSPA), the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), the National Property Data System and regulated housing development accounts.

items.title: More arrests possible in MyIMMs hacking probe, says MACC chief
items.summary: MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the number of people involved could be considered substantial, with investigations ongoing to determine the extent of their involvement. "The operation involved the MACC Intelligence Division's Special Project Branch, together with the Immigration Department Intelligence Division, Securities Commission Malaysia, Telekom Malaysia, National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa), and the MACC Technology Forensics Division. He said those detained comprised two company directors, three foreign nationals, four Immigration Department officers, two officers from the Immigration Department's Information Technology Division, and a police officer.

items.title: Nga: Big data platform to fix housing supply mismatch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is developing a big data analytics platform that will allow private developers to make more informed housing decisions and address the mismatch between supply and market demand. Nga said the platform would help ensure housing projects better match buyers' needs, adding that Malaysia's housing sector did not face a supply shortage but a mismatch between available homes and market demand. Nga said the ministry was also studying the housing needs of the M40 income group to ensure future housing products better reflect market requirements.

items.title: Foreign automakers must help build Malaysia's auto ecosystem, says Johari
items.summary: TANJUNG MALIM: Foreign automakers investing in Malaysia must go beyond selling vehicles and instead contribute to the development of the country's automotive ecosystem, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said. Today, Proton's tax contribution has reached RM806 million. This comes from corporate tax, excise duty, import duty and sales tax.

items.title: Malaysia hits 34.4 million population; Selangor largest, Terengganu fastest-growing as 12 states enter ageing status, says Stats Dept
items.summary: The citizens’ population rose from 30.8 million in 2025 to 31 million in 2026, recording a growth rate of 0.6 per cent, while the non-citizen population declined by 0.2 per cent. At state level, Terengganu recorded the highest population growth rate at 1.2 per cent, followed by Kelantan at 1 per cent, while Selangor, Putrajaya and Pahang each recorded growth of 0.6 per cent. DOSM said the proportion of children aged 0 to 14 years declined from 21.6 per cent in 2025 to 21.2 per cent in 2026, while the working-age population aged 15 to 64 remained unchanged at 70.4 per cent.

items.title: Anwar extends birthday wishes to Sultan of Pahang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his heartfelt birthday wishes to the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, on His Royal Highness's 67th birthday. In a Facebook post today, Anwar prayed that the Sultan and the Pahang Royal Family would continue to receive Allah's blessings, guidance, good health, wellbeing and enduring sovereignty. "Daulat Tuanku, Dirgahayu Tuanku," he posted.

items.title: Coal mine blast kills at least 34 in Pakistan
items.summary: QUETTA, Pakistan: A blast at a coal mine killed at least 34 workers in southern Pakistan, the provincial disaster agency said on Friday, adding rescuers were searching for more missing miners. "According to information received from the deployed teams, 34x Dead bodies have been recovered," southern Balochistan's provincial disaster management authority said in a statement in the early hours of Friday. Mining accidents are common in Pakistan, particularly in Balochistan.

items.title: SUV driver pleads not guilty to causing deaths of three family members in Hulu Langat crash after meth-positive test
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — A labourer pleaded not guilty at the Magistrates’ Court in Kajang today to three charges of driving under the influence of drugs, causing the deaths of three family members last Wednesday. According to Utusan Malaysia , Mohd Norazlan Mohd Tamyiz, 42, entered his plea after all three charges were read before Magistrate Fatin Dayana Jalil. Under the charges, he was accused of driving a sport utility vehicle (SUV) while under the influence of methamphetamine, resulting in the deaths of three individuals.

items.title: Eight arrested over alleged online travel scam targeting China, Taiwan
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Eight foreigners allegedly operating an online travel scam targeting victims in China and Taiwan were arrested after police raided a luxury condominium in Tanjung Bungah yesterday. Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the suspects, comprising seven foreign men and a woman aged between 25 and 37, were arrested inside the condominium unit. "Initial investigations found the syndicate allegedly offered online travel packages to Japan to victims in China and Taiwan," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Climbing legend Nirmal Purja among 10 missing after Pakistan avalanche
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja is among 10 people missing after an avalanche in northern Pakistan where they were on a climbing expedition, the country's alpine club said. "The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) has received deeply concerning reports of an avalanche that struck a team of climbers on Broad Peak (8,047m) in the Karakoram mountain range," the club said late on Thursday, adding that the team led by Purja could not be reached since the incident. "The entire team has reportedly been out of communication since the avalanche," the club said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Stray dog dies during Port Klang capture operation after public interference
items.summary: PORT KLANG: A stray dog died during a capture operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah after Majlis Bandaraya Diraja Klang personnel released the loop equipment being used following an incident involving members of the public. The council said in a statement that the operation involved 11 staff members, a Health Department officer and about 50 residents. It said 12 stray dogs were captured using loop equipment that complied with standards set by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government, with the process carried out while prioritising animal welfare.

items.title: From recycled glass to miniature worlds: Syukur's terrarium passion blooms
items.summary: JELI: A hobby of creating terrariums from recycled glass containers and second-hand items has blossomed into a creative passion for Muhammad Syukur Abdullah, 21, who now crafts intricate miniature garden landscapes. The second-semester Aquaculture Technology Diploma student at Jeli Polytechnic said his interest began during his secondary school years after watching a YouTube video that inspired him to create his own terrarium. My interest continued to grow, leading me to pursue an Aquaculture Technology Certificate at Jerantut Community College, Pahang, in 2022," he told Bernama at Jeli Polytechnic yesterday.

items.title: Anwar hails Al-Azhar Grand Imam Al-Tayyeb as global moderation icon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed his high appreciation for the Grand Imam of Al-Azhar Al-Sharif, Prof Dr Ahmad Muhammad Ahmad Al-Tayyeb, who was described as one of the most vocal figures advocating the wasatiyyah (moderation) approach in addressing current issues. Anwar, in the book “In the Presence of Al-Tayeb” as quoted by the official Facebook page of Al-Azhar Al-Sharif, said the prominent scholar had called for greater efforts to strengthen unity among the ummah, nurture values of compassion and love, mutual respect, and promote harmonious coexistence between Muslims and non-Muslims. According to Anwar, besides his role in the Islamic world, Al-Tayyeb has also played a significant role in strengthening interfaith dialogue.

items.title: MACC begins Tabung Haji RCI probe, sends eight officers to review documents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has begun investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH), with eight officers deployed to the institution’s headquarters today to obtain and review relevant documents. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigation was launched following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s call for enforcement agencies to take appropriate action based on the findings of the recently released RCI report, according to a Berita Harian report. “The investigation team began work this morning by identifying documents related to matters highlighted in the RCI report, as well as issues that are linked to our investigation.

items.title: Two 16-year-olds detained over alleged rape of underage girl in Jertih
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Two 16-year-old boys have been detained to assist investigations into the alleged rape of a teenage girl at a lodging facility in Jertih yesterday. Besut district police chief Superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said police received a report regarding the alleged rape involving a 15-year-old girl, Harian Metro reported. “Following that, police detained two male suspects aged 16 at about 2.30am today in Jertih to assist investigations,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: N. Sembilan polls: EC expects full results before midnight on Saturday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — The Election Commission (EC) expects the full results of the Negeri Sembilan state election to be announced before midnight, with preliminary results likely to be available from around 10pm on Saturday. Sinar Harian reported that EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the target was achievable as preparations for polling had reached an optimal stage, with ballot box checks completed at all polling centres. He said the EC had inspected the ballot box verification process at Dewan Perdana Tampin today, while ensuring all polling centres statewide were ready for polling day.

items.title: King extends Warriors Day greetings to Armed Forces, police personnel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today extended his Warriors Day greetings to all personnel of the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) and Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). “Happy Warriors Day. Warriors Day is observed annually to honour the sacrifices and contributions of members of the country’s security forces.

items.title: N. Sembilan polls: Pakatan aiming for minimum 19 seats, says Amirudin
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, July 31 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has set its sights on securing at least 19 seats in the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election this Saturday, said its election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. Amirudin said he was confident that Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun’s leadership as Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar, coupled with PH’s two-term track record in administering the state, would give the coalition an advantage. He said PH would instead continue to highlight the Malaysia Madani agenda and unity among the people as its message to voters.

items.title: Selangor Speaker to clarify assemblyman’s status on Aug 3, says MB
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, July 31 – The Selangor State Assembly Speaker is expected to announce on Monday (August 3) the outcome of a review into allegations concerning the status of a state assemblyman, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said. He said he was consulting the State Legal Adviser to verify the allegations before any further action is taken. “We have received information regarding the matter and are currently consulting the State Legal Advisor.

items.title: King to undergo follow-up treatment for back, hip pain
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, will undergo follow-up treatment for musculoskeletal pain involving his back and hip areas. In a statement today, Istana Negara said His Majesty had been advised by medical specialists to rest before undergoing further treatment to allow the recovery process to take place. As a result, Sultan Ibrahim did not attend the National Heroes Day Parade at Dataran Pahlawan Negara, Putrajaya today.

items.title: Fahmi: ‘Sakau’ term not in Tabung Haji RCI report, but corrupt practices clear
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, July 31 — Governance and integrity should be the key considerations for voters when choosing their leaders in the 16th Negeri Sembilan polls to ensure the nation’s key institutions are not further undermined by corruption and abuse of power, said Pakatan Harapan (PH) communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Citing the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Fahmi said the issue should serve as a lesson, given the damaging consequences of weak governance and abuse of power. He said that although the official RCI report submitted to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong did not use colloquial terms such as sakau (to loot or embezzle), it clearly revealed acts of corruption and misappropriation.
